revision:
1. Visual Metaphor & Execution: Retain the core duality of 'Blue Hour' (calm) vs. 'Red Noise' (chaos). Replace the sterile, default smooth sine wave with an organic, hand-drawn vector path to inject 'live' improvisational energy. Replace the flat, pixelated red overlay with a sharp, high-contrast jagged 'sawtooth' SVG path that structurally erupts from the end of the blue line. Apply a directional red rim-light/glow to the spikes to simulate sonic impact and volume, avoiding generic drop shadows or low-res texture filters.

2. Composition & Hierarchy: Establish a dynamic diagonal visual path. Keep the title 'BLUE HOUR RED NOISE' as the unobstructed, dominant focal point at the top. Align the left margin of the bottom-left logistical text block (Date/Venue) to the specific angle of the blue wave’s initial ascent. This creates a diagonal grid that implies movement and syncopation without curving the text, ensuring the eye travels from the date, up the wave, into the red noise, and finally to the title.

3. Typography & Integration: Replace the generic headline font with an aggressive, condensed sans-serif to mimic verticality and urban density. Apply a subtle horizontal shear or motion blur effect specifically to the 'RED NOISE' portion of the headline to visually echo the jagged waveform, while keeping 'BLUE HOUR' clean. Ensure performer names ('Nia Cole Quartet', 'Static Bloom', 'Armand Vale') remain strictly horizontal, legible, and undistorted, supporting the hierarchy without competing for attention.

4. Color & Atmosphere: Maintain the high-contrast Cyan/Red palette against a dark background. Replace heavy, uniform drop shadows with subtle directional ambient occlusion (dark grey) and faint colored rim lights on text edges to integrate typography into the scene's lighting model. Ensure the transition from blue to red feels like a natural degradation of signal rather than a digital error, preserving the 'experimental jazz' atmosphere.
protected_strengths: The color-coded duality of Blue (smooth/calm) vs. Red (chaotic/noise) as the central visual anchor.
The diagonal trajectory of the waveform which creates inherent movement and leads the eye.
The clear distinction between the headline as the primary identity and performer names as secondary, legible information.
resolved_conflicts: Conflict: Organic vs. Geometric Waveform -> Resolution: Use organic/hand-drawn vectors for the blue 'Blue Hour' section to convey live energy, but retain sharp, geometric jaggedness for the red 'Red Noise' section to convey structural tension and clarity.

Conflict: Text Integration vs. Legibility -> Resolution: Reject curving text (illegible) and static blocks (boring). Instead, align the left margin of the text block to the wave's angle, creating a diagonal grid that implies rhythm while maintaining horizontal readability for performer names.

Conflict: Glitch Effects vs. Visual Clutter -> Resolution: Reject full-text glitching. Apply distortion/shear only to the 'RED NOISE' headline text to mirror the graphic, keeping the rest of the typography clean to preserve the single focal point of chaos.

Conflict: Depth/Shadows vs. Sterile Look -> Resolution: Reject generic drop shadows. Use directional ambient occlusion and colored rim lighting to integrate text into the atmospheric lighting of the poster without reducing legibility.
rationale: This brief prioritizes the 'Visual Concept' by refining the metaphor from a digital error to a physical sonic event. It resolves 'Composition' conflicts by using alignment rather than rotation to create movement, preserving legibility. 'Typography' is treated as expressive material through selective distortion, and 'Color/Craft' is elevated by replacing generic effects with integrated lighting models. All four mandates are weighted equally by ensuring the visual metaphor drives the composition, which in turn dictates the typographic treatment and atmospheric finish.
